paper.title: BISTRO: An Efficient Relaxation-Based Method for Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with i.i.d. covariates and arbitrary cost sequences (hybrid i.i.d.-adversarial)
unmapped: Contexts i.i.d. from unknown P_x, but learner can draw samples from P_x (unlabeled data)
Arbitrary (possibly uncountable) policy class F of maps X -> [d], accessed via a value-of-ERM oracle
Bound depends on vector-valued Rademacher complexity of F
settings.definition_quote: On each round $t=1,\ldots,n$, we observe covariates $x_t\in\X$, select an action $\pred_t\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and observe the cost $c_t(\pred_t)$ ... We assume that $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are drawn i.i.d. from some unknown distribution $P_x$ on $\X$. At the same time, we do not place any assumption on the sequence of costs $c_1,\ldots,c_n$

unmapped: Requires an admissible full-information relaxation for the policy class F
Bound in terms of full-information relaxation value Rel^dagger(empty)
settings.definition_quote: Suppose we place no assumption on the evolution of $x_t$'s, which may now be treated as worst-case.

symbols.Rad_F: expected vector-valued Rademacher complexity E Rad(F; x_{1:n}) of the policy class

conditions: learner can sample contexts from P_x (unlabeled data)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: The partial-information relaxation ... is admissible. An admissible randomized strategy for this relaxation is given by BISTRO (Algorithm~\ref{alg}). The expected regret of the algorithm with $\gamma=\sqrt{2\En\Rad(\F;x_{1:n})/(nd)}$ is upper bounded by $$2\sqrt{2d \cdot n \cdot \En\Rad(\F;x_{1:n})}.$$

results.notes: Paper's d = number of actions (K), n = T. Requires d ERM-value oracle calls per round. For finite F the intro states O(n^{3/4}(log|F|)^{1/4}). Also holds for data-dependent classes F[x_{1:n}]. Tuning requires E Rad.

symbols.Rad_Mtilde: expected Rademacher complexity of relaxed superset of matrices M~ containing the policy matrices

conditions: M~ contains the policy matrices and has column sums <= 1
learner can sample contexts from P_x

source.label: lem:opt_relaxation
source.quote: Let $\widetilde{\cM}\supseteq\Mhat$ be a set of matrices such that the column sum $\sum_{j=1}^d M_t(j) \leq 1$ ... BISTRO (with ERM over $\widetilde{\cM}$ rather than $\cM$) is an admissible strategy for this relaxation and the expected regret is upper bounded by $$2\sqrt{2d\cdot n\cdot \En\Rad(\widetilde{\cM})}.$$

results.notes: Variant of BISTRO using an optimization-based relaxation (LP/SDP) of the ERM; comparator still F.

symbols.Rel_full: initial value Rel^dagger(empty) of an admissible full-information relaxation for F

conditions: an admissible full-information relaxation exists for F
tuning: q_t = (1-d gamma) q_t^* + gamma 1 with gamma optimized

source.label: lem:if_full_then_partial
source.quote: If $\Relfull{}{}$ is an admissible full-information relaxation for the adversarial scenario, then $$\Rel{}{I_{1:t}} \deq \gamma^{-1}\Relfull{}{\gamma\tilde{c}_{1},\ldots,\gamma\tilde{c}_t}+(n-t)d\gamma$$ is admissible ... The resulting regret upper bound is $$2\sqrt{d \cdot n \cdot \Relfull{}{\emptyset}}.$$

results.notes: The gamma choice is implicit; computational complexity equals that of the full-information procedure.
